passages.text: On the fifteenth day of the second month after they had left the land of Egypt, the whole congregation of Israel set out from Elim and came to the Desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel had left Egypt.
They traveled together as a whole congregation.
They set out from a place called Elim.
They came to the Desert of Sin.
This desert is between Elim and Sinai.
They arrived there on the fifteenth day of the second month after leaving Egypt.
passages.original: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מֵֽאֵילִ֔ם וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ כָּל־ עֲדַ֤ת בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־ מִדְבַּר־ סִ֔ין אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֵּין־ אֵילִ֖ם וּבֵ֣ין סִינָ֑י בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֨ה עָשָׂ֥ר יוֹם֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י לְצֵאתָ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: And there in the desert they all grumbled against Moses and Aaron.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were in the desert.
The Israelites were a large group of people.
The Israelites were the descendants of Jacob.
The Israelites had left Egypt.
The Israelites all complained.
They complained about Moses.
They complained about Aaron.
They grumbled against Moses and Aaron in the desert.
passages.original: וַיִּלִּינוּ כָּל־ עֲדַ֧ת בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עַל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְעַֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֖ן בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

passages.text: “If only we had died by the LORD’s hand in the land of Egypt!” they said. “There we sat by pots of meat and ate our fill of bread, but you have brought us into this desert to starve this whole assembly to death!”
passages.sermon:
The Israelites spoke to Moses and Aaron.
They said, “We wish the LORD had let us die in Egypt.
In Egypt, we sat by pots filled with meat.
We ate bread until we were full.
But you brought us into this desert.
You brought all these people here to die from hunger.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ אֲלֵהֶ֜ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מִֽי־ יִתֵּ֨ן מוּתֵ֤נוּ בְיַד־ יְהוָה֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּשִׁבְתֵּ֙נוּ֙ עַל־ סִ֣יר הַבָּשָׂ֔ר בְּאָכְלֵ֥נוּ לֶ֖חֶם לָשֹׂ֑בַע כִּֽי־ הוֹצֵאתֶ֤ם אֹתָ֙נוּ֙ אֶל־ הַמִּדְבָּ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה לְהָמִ֛ית אֶת־ כָּל־ הַקָּהָ֥ל הַזֶּ֖ה בָּרָעָֽב׃ס

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Behold, I will rain down bread from heaven for you. Each day the people are to go out and gather enough for that day. In this way I will test whether or not they will follow My instructions.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD said, “I will send bread from heaven for you.
I will make it fall like rain.
The people must go out each day.
They must gather enough bread for that day.
I will do this to test the people.
I will see if they obey My instructions or not.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה הִנְנִ֨י מַמְטִ֥יר לָכֶ֛ם לֶ֖חֶם מִן־ הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְיָצָ֨א הָעָ֤ם וְלָֽקְטוּ֙ דְּבַר־ י֣וֹם בְּיוֹמ֔וֹ לְמַ֧עַן אֲנַסֶּ֛נּוּ הֲיֵלֵ֥ךְ בְּתוֹרָתִ֖י אִם־ לֹֽא׃

passages.text: Then on the sixth day, when they prepare what they bring in, it will be twice as much as they gather on the other days.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave instructions to the Israelites.
God said, “On the sixth day, the people must gather food.
They must prepare what they bring in on that day.
On the sixth day, the amount will be double.
This will be twice as much as they gather on the other days.”
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁ֔י וְהֵכִ֖ינוּ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־ יָבִ֑יאוּ וְהָיָ֣ה מִשְׁנֶ֔ה עַ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר־ יִלְקְט֖וּ י֥וֹם׀ יֽוֹם׃ס

passages.text: So Moses and Aaron said to all the Israelites, “This evening you will know that it was the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt, and in the morning you will see the LORD’s glory, because He has heard your grumbling against Him. For who are we that you should grumble against us?”
passages.sermon:
Moses and Aaron spoke to all the Israelites.
They said, “This evening you will know something important.
You will know that the LORD brought you out of the land of Egypt.
In the morning you will see the LORD’s glory.
The LORD has heard your grumbling against Him.
We are not important.
Why do you grumble against us?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ וְאַהֲרֹ֔ן אֶֽל־ כָּל־ בְּנֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עֶ֕רֶב וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֧י יְהוָ֛ה הוֹצִ֥יא אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃ וּבֹ֗קֶר וּרְאִיתֶם֙ אֶת־ כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֔ה בְּשָׁמְע֥וֹ אֶת־ תְּלֻנֹּתֵיכֶ֖ם עַל־ יְהוָ֑ה וְנַ֣חְנוּ מָ֔ה כִּ֥י תַלּוֹנוּ עָלֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: And Moses added, “The LORD will give you meat to eat this evening and bread to fill you in the morning, for He has heard your grumbling against Him. Who are we? Your grumblings are not against us but against the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the Israelites.
He said, "The LORD will give you meat to eat this evening.
He will give you bread in the morning so you will be full.
The LORD has heard your grumbling against Him.
You are complaining against the LORD.
We are not the ones you are complaining about.
Your grumbling is against the LORD, not against us."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה בְּתֵ֣ת יְהוָה֩ לָכֶ֨ם בָּעֶ֜רֶב בָּשָׂ֣ר לֶאֱכֹ֗ל וְלֶ֤חֶם בַּבֹּ֙קֶר֙ לִשְׂבֹּ֔עַ בִּשְׁמֹ֤עַ יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ תְּלֻנֹּ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־ אַתֶּ֥ם מַלִּינִ֖ם עָלָ֑יו וְנַ֣חְנוּ מָ֔ה לֹא־ עָלֵ֥ינוּ תְלֻנֹּתֵיכֶ֖ם כִּ֥י עַל־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Then Moses said to Aaron, “Tell the whole congregation of Israel, ‘Come before the LORD, for He has heard your grumbling.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
Aaron was Moses’ brother and helper.
Moses spoke to Aaron.
Moses gave Aaron a command.
Moses told Aaron to speak to all the Israelites.
Moses said, “Tell the whole congregation of Israel, ‘Come before the LORD.’”
Moses said, “The LORD has heard your grumbling.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֔ן אֱמֹ֗ר אֶֽל־ כָּל־ עֲדַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל קִרְב֖וּ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֔ע אֵ֖ת תְּלֻנֹּתֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: And as Aaron was speaking to the whole congregation of Israel, they looked toward the desert, and there in a cloud the glory of the LORD appeared.
passages.sermon:
Aaron was a leader of Israel.
Aaron spoke to all the people of Israel.
The people of Israel listened to Aaron.
The people of Israel turned and looked toward the desert.
A cloud was in the desert.
The glory of the LORD appeared in the cloud.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כְּדַבֵּ֤ר אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶל־ כָּל־ עֲדַ֣ת בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּפְנ֖וּ אֶל־ הַמִּדְבָּ֑ר וְהִנֵּה֙ כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֔ה נִרְאָ֖ה בֶּעָנָֽן׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “I have heard the grumbling of the Israelites. Tell them, ‘At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be filled with bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD said, “I have heard the complaints of the Israelites.”
The LORD told Moses to speak to the people.
The LORD said, “Tell them this.”
“At twilight you will eat meat.”
“In the morning you will have all the bread you want.”
“Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.”
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי אֶת־ תְּלוּנֹּת֮ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ דַּבֵּ֨ר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר בֵּ֤ין הָֽעַרְבַּ֙יִם֙ תֹּאכְל֣וּ בָשָׂ֔ר וּבַבֹּ֖קֶר תִּשְׂבְּעוּ־ לָ֑חֶם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: That evening quail came and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.
passages.sermon:
God led the Israelites in the wilderness.
The Israelites camped in the desert.
That evening, quail came.
The quail covered the camp.
In the morning, dew appeared.
The dew formed a layer around the camp.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י בָעֶ֔רֶב וַתַּ֣עַל הַשְּׂלָ֔ו וַתְּכַ֖ס אֶת־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וּבַבֹּ֗קֶר הָֽיְתָה֙ שִׁכְבַ֣ת הַטַּ֔ל סָבִ֖יב לַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

passages.text: When the layer of dew had evaporated, there were thin flakes on the desert floor, as fine as frost on the ground.
passages.sermon:
God led the Israelites through the desert.
In the morning, a layer of dew covered the ground around their camp.
The dew evaporated.
Thin flakes appeared on the surface of the desert.
These flakes were very fine.
They were as fine as frost on the ground.
passages.original: וַתַּ֖עַל שִׁכְבַ֣ת הַטָּ֑ל וְהִנֵּ֞ה עַל־ פְּנֵ֤י הַמִּדְבָּר֙ דַּ֣ק מְחֻסְפָּ֔ס דַּ֥ק כַּכְּפֹ֖ר עַל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: When the Israelites saw it, they asked one another, “What is it?” For they did not know what it was. So Moses told them, “It is the bread that the LORD has given you to eat.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites saw something on the ground.
They did not know what it was.
Each person asked his brother, “What is it?”
They were confused because they did not recognize it.
Moses spoke to them.
Moses said, “This is the bread.”
Moses said, “The LORD has given this bread to you.”
Moses said, “God gave it to you to eat.”
passages.original: וַיִּרְא֣וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ אִ֤ישׁ אֶל־ אָחִיו֙ מָ֣ן ה֔וּא כִּ֛י לֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ מַה־ ה֑וּא וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם ה֣וּא הַלֶּ֔חֶם אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה לָכֶ֖ם לְאָכְלָֽה׃

passages.text: This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Each one is to gather as much as he needs. You may take an omer for each person in your tent.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD gave a command.
Each person must gather food.
Each person must gather as much as he needs to eat.
Each person must take one omer for each person in his tent.
Each person must count the people in his tent.
Each person must gather for everyone in his tent.
passages.original: זֶ֤ה הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה לִקְט֣וּ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ אִ֖ישׁ לְפִ֣י אָכְל֑וֹ עֹ֣מֶר לַגֻּלְגֹּ֗לֶת מִסְפַּר֙ נַפְשֹׁ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם אִ֛ישׁ לַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּאָהֳל֖וֹ תִּקָּֽחוּ׃

passages.text: So the Israelites did this. Some gathered more, and some less.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites obeyed God.
They gathered the bread.
Some Israelites gathered a lot.
Some Israelites gathered a little.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲשׂוּ־ כֵ֖ן בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיִּלְקְט֔וּ הַמַּרְבֶּ֖ה וְהַמַּמְעִֽיט׃

passages.text: When they measured it by the omer, he who gathered much had no excess, and he who gathered little had no shortfall. Each one gathered as much as he needed to eat.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites gathered manna in the wilderness.
They measured what they gathered using an omer.
Anyone who gathered much did not have extra.
Anyone who gathered little did not lack.
Each person gathered exactly what he needed to eat.
passages.original: וַיָּמֹ֣דּוּ בָעֹ֔מֶר וְלֹ֤א הֶעְדִּיף֙ הַמַּרְבֶּ֔ה וְהַמַּמְעִ֖יט לֹ֣א הֶחְסִ֑יר אִ֥ישׁ לְפִֽי־ אָכְל֖וֹ לָקָֽטוּ׃

passages.text: Then Moses said to them, “No one may keep any of it until morning.”
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
Moses spoke to the Israelites.
Moses gave them a command.
Moses said, “No one may keep any of the manna until morning.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֲלֵהֶ֑ם אִ֕ישׁ אַל־ יוֹתֵ֥ר מִמֶּ֖נּוּ עַד־ בֹּֽקֶר׃

passages.text: But they did not listen to Moses; some people left part of it until morning, and it became infested with maggots and began to smell. So Moses was angry with them.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites did not listen to Moses.
Some people kept some of the manna until morning.
Maggots grew in the manna.
The manna began to smell bad.
Moses became angry with those people.
passages.original: וְלֹא־ שָׁמְע֣וּ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיּוֹתִ֨רוּ אֲנָשִׁ֤ים מִמֶּ֙נּוּ֙ עַד־ בֹּ֔קֶר וַיָּ֥רֻם תּוֹלָעִ֖ים וַיִּבְאַ֑שׁ וַיִּקְצֹ֥ף עֲלֵהֶ֖ם מֹשֶֽׁה׃

passages.text: Every morning each one gathered as much as was needed, and when the sun grew hot, it melted away.
passages.sermon: The Israelites gathered manna every morning.\r\nEach person took as much as he needed for food.\r\nWhen the sun became hot, the manna melted away.
passages.original: וַיִּלְקְט֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֔קֶר אִ֖ישׁ כְּפִ֣י אָכְל֑וֹ וְחַ֥ם הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ וְנָמָֽס׃

passages.text: On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much food—two omers per person —and all the leaders of the congregation came and reported this to Moses.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were in the wilderness.
God provided them with food called manna.
On the sixth day, the people gathered food.
They gathered twice as much as usual.
Each person collected two omers.
All the leaders of the congregation saw this.
The leaders came to Moses.
The leaders reported this to Moses.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁ֗י לָֽקְט֥וּ לֶ֙חֶם֙ מִשְׁנֶ֔ה שְׁנֵ֥י הָעֹ֖מֶר לָאֶחָ֑ד וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ כָּל־ נְשִׂיאֵ֣י הָֽעֵדָ֔ה וַיַּגִּ֖ידוּ לְמֹשֶֽׁה׃

passages.text: He told them, “This is what the LORD has said: ‘Tomorrow is to be a day of complete rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. So bake what you want to bake, and boil what you want to boil. Then set aside whatever remains and keep it until morning.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the people.
He said, “The LORD has given a command.
Tomorrow will be a day of complete rest.
Tomorrow will be a holy Sabbath to the LORD.
Bake what you want to bake today.
Boil what you want to boil today.
Set aside all the food that is left over.
Keep the leftover food until morning.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם ה֚וּא אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שַׁבָּת֧וֹן שַׁבַּת־ קֹ֛דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָ֖ה מָחָ֑ר אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־ תֹּאפ֞וּ אֵפ֗וּ וְאֵ֤ת אֲשֶֽׁר־ תְּבַשְּׁלוּ֙ בַּשֵּׁ֔לוּ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־ הָ֣עֹדֵ֔ף הַנִּ֧יחוּ לָכֶ֛ם לְמִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת עַד־ הַבֹּֽקֶר׃

passages.text: So they set it aside until morning as Moses had commanded, and it did not smell or contain any maggots.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites gathered manna in the wilderness.
Moses was their leader.
Moses gave them a command.
He told them to set aside the manna until morning.
They obeyed Moses.
They kept the manna until morning.
The manna did not smell bad.
No maggots appeared in it.
passages.original: וַיַּנִּ֤יחוּ אֹתוֹ֙ עַד־ הַבֹּ֔קֶר כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֣ה מֹשֶׁ֑ה וְלֹ֣א הִבְאִ֔ישׁ וְרִמָּ֖ה לֹא־ הָ֥יְתָה בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: “Eat it today,” Moses said, “because today is a Sabbath to the LORD. Today you will not find anything in the field.
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the people.
He told them to eat the food today.
Today is the Sabbath.
The Sabbath is a holy day for the LORD.
You will not find food in the field today.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אִכְלֻ֣הוּ הַיּ֔וֹם כִּֽי־ שַׁבָּ֥ת הַיּ֖וֹם לַיהוָ֑ה הַיּ֕וֹם לֹ֥א תִמְצָאֻ֖הוּ בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃

passages.text: For six days you may gather, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, it will not be there.”
passages.sermon:
God gave the Israelites manna to eat in the wilderness.
God told the Israelites to gather manna for food.
You may gather manna for six days.
The seventh day is the Sabbath.
On the Sabbath, manna will not be there.
You will not find manna on the seventh day.
passages.original: שֵׁ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים תִּלְקְטֻ֑הוּ וּבַיּ֧וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֛י שַׁבָּ֖ת לֹ֥א יִֽהְיֶה־ בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Yet on the seventh day some of the people went out to gather, but they did not find anything.
passages.sermon:
Some people belonged to Israel.
The seventh day arrived.
Some people went out.
They tried to gather food.
They did not find anything.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י יָצְא֥וּ מִן־ הָעָ֖ם לִלְקֹ֑ט וְלֹ֖א מָצָֽאוּ׃ס

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “How long will you refuse to keep My commandments and instructions?
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD asked a question.
The LORD said, "How long will you refuse to obey My commandments?
How long will you refuse to follow My instructions?"
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֑ה עַד־ אָ֙נָה֙ מֵֽאַנְתֶּ֔ם לִשְׁמֹ֥ר מִצְוֺתַ֖י וְתוֹרֹתָֽי׃

passages.text: Understand that the LORD has given you the Sabbath; that is why on the sixth day He will give you bread for two days. On the seventh day, everyone must stay where he is; no one may leave his place.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD gave you the Sabbath.
The Sabbath is a day of rest.
The LORD provides for your needs.
On the sixth day, the LORD gives you bread for two days.
This bread is enough for both the sixth and seventh days.
On the seventh day, you must stay where you are.
No one should leave his place on the seventh day.
passages.original: רְא֗וּ כִּֽי־ יְהוָה֮ נָתַ֣ן לָכֶ֣ם הַשַּׁבָּת֒ עַל־ כֵּ֠ן ה֣וּא נֹתֵ֥ן לָכֶ֛ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁ֖י לֶ֣חֶם יוֹמָ֑יִם שְׁב֣וּ׀ אִ֣ישׁ תַּחְתָּ֗יו אַל־ יֵ֥צֵא אִ֛ישׁ מִמְּקֹמ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִֽי׃

passages.text: So the people rested on the seventh day.
passages.sermon: The people of Israel stopped their work.\r\nThey rested on the seventh day.\r\nThey obeyed God's command to rest on the Sabbath.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁבְּת֥וּ הָעָ֖ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִעִֽי׃

passages.text: Now the house of Israel called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel called the bread "manna".
The manna was white.
It looked like coriander seed.
The manna tasted like wafers made with honey.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרְא֧וּ בֵֽית־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת־ שְׁמ֖וֹ מָ֑ן וְה֗וּא כְּזֶ֤רַע גַּד֙ לָבָ֔ן וְטַעְמ֖וֹ כְּצַפִּיחִ֥ת בִּדְבָֽשׁ׃

passages.text: Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Keep an omer of manna for the generations to come, so that they may see the bread I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the people.
Moses said, “The LORD gave a command.
The LORD said to keep an omer of manna.
Keep it for your descendants.
This will be for all generations to come.
They will see the bread I gave you.
I fed you with this bread in the wilderness.
I did this when I brought you out of Egypt.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה זֶ֤ה הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה מְלֹ֤א הָעֹ֙מֶר֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ לְמִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶ֑ם לְמַ֣עַן׀ יִרְא֣וּ אֶת־ הַלֶּ֗חֶם אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֶאֱכַ֤לְתִּי אֶתְכֶם֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר בְּהוֹצִיאִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: So Moses told Aaron, “Take a jar and fill it with an omer of manna. Then place it before the LORD to be preserved for the generations to come.”
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Aaron was Moses’ brother and helper.
Moses spoke to Aaron.
Moses gave Aaron a command.
Moses said, “Take one jar.”
Moses said, “Fill the jar with an omer of manna.”
Manna was the bread God gave Israel in the wilderness.
Moses said, “Put the jar before the LORD.”
Moses said, “Keep it safe for your descendants.”
Moses wanted future generations to see the manna.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֗ן קַ֚ח צִנְצֶ֣נֶת אַחַ֔ת וְתֶן־ שָׁ֥מָּה מְלֹֽא־ הָעֹ֖מֶר מָ֑ן וְהַנַּ֤ח אֹתוֹ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לְמִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: And Aaron placed it in front of the Testimony, to be preserved just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
passages.sermon:
Aaron was the brother of Moses.
God gave Moses a command.
God told Moses to preserve manna.
Aaron obeyed God’s command.
Aaron took the manna.
Aaron placed the manna in front of the Testimony.
The Testimony was a sacred place.
Aaron put the manna there to keep it safe.
Aaron did this so future generations could see it.
Aaron did everything just as God told Moses.
passages.original: כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיַּנִּיחֵ֧הוּ אַהֲרֹ֛ן לִפְנֵ֥י הָעֵדֻ֖ת לְמִשְׁמָֽרֶת׃

passages.text: The Israelites ate manna forty years, until they came to a land where they could settle; they ate manna until they reached the border of Canaan.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites wandered in the wilderness.
God provided food for them.
God gave them manna to eat.
The Israelites ate manna for forty years.
They ate manna until they reached a land where they could live.
They ate manna until they came to the border of Canaan.
passages.original: וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָֽכְל֤וּ אֶת־ הַמָּן֙ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה עַד־ בֹּאָ֖ם אֶל־ אֶ֣רֶץ נוֹשָׁ֑בֶת אֶת־ הַמָּן֙ אָֽכְל֔וּ עַד־ בֹּאָ֕ם אֶל־ קְצֵ֖ה אֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃

passages.text: (Now an omer is a tenth of an ephah.)
passages.sermon: An omer is a unit of measure.\r\nAn omer equals one tenth of an ephah.
passages.original: וְהָעֹ֕מֶר עֲשִׂרִ֥ית הָאֵיפָ֖ה הֽוּא׃פ
